extracted.intended_audience: agency managers, policymakers, administrative-law researchers and analysts tracking agency adjudication workload and disposition outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Statistical tables summarizing proceedings pending before agency examiners in FY1957: counts by proceeding type and agency, dispositions, use of shortened procedures, and time-to-decision buckets. The document is used to analyze backlog, procedural outcomes, and processing times across 21 agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlog and volume data (start/new/remanded/disposed/end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Columns capturing case counts: 'No. of cases pending July 1, 1956'; 'New cases asgn'd during 1957'; 'Old cases remanded during 1957'; 'Cases disposed of by ex'mrs during 1957'; 'No. of cases pending June 30, 1957'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure inflow, outflow, and net backlog change for each type of proceeding and agency. Footnotes note that some input may include cases assigned prior to July 1, 1956 and that data limitations may affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of proceedings reported by agencies (statutory categories / rows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rows list specific types of proceedings (e.g., 'Certificates of convenience and necessity, 49 U.S.C. ...', 'Cease and desist orders, 15 U.S.C. 21, 45...', 'Appeals from benefit rights determinations, 42 U.S.C. 405', etc.) organized under each reporting agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each row is a distinct proceeding category (with statutory citation) for which the volume and disposition metrics are reported; comparisons and totals are broken down by these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition (disposition categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition categories reported: 'Ex'mrs. decision on the merits'; 'Dismissal on procedural grounds'; 'Voluntary Withdrawal'; 'Removal from ex'mr. for Agency Action'; 'Other'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table II and continuations break dispositions into these categories and further show whether the disposition occurred 'Before Hearing' or 'After Hearing'. Useful for analyzing how cases are terminated and the relative frequency of merits decisions vs procedural or other terminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing timing for dispositions (before/after hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each disposition category, counts are split into 'Before Hearing' and 'After Hearing' (i.e., whether the disposition occurred prior to an evidentiary hearing or following one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables assessment of how many cases are resolved without a hearing versus after a hearing; cross-tabulated with disposition type (merits, dismissal, withdrawal, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of proceedings pending (pending-before-examiner aging buckets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table III categorizes pending cases by time already pending before examiners: '3 mos. or less', '3 to 6 months', '6 to 12 months', 'Over 12 months', along with totals 'Total cases pending June 30, 1957'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show backlog aging and identify categories/ agencies with long-pending matters. Footnotes explain special counting practices for some agencies (e.g., counting from date set for hearing vs assignment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'shortened procedures' (decisions without evidentiary hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics showing for each proceeding: 'Total cases disposed of by ex'mrs. during the year'; 'No. of cases decided on the merits after oral hearing'; 'No. of cases decided on the merits by shortened procedure'; 'Other disposition'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report defines shortened procedures as permitting examiners to issue decisions on the merits without evidentiary hearings (i.e., decided on written submissions only). Table IV quantifies how often shortened procedures are used by proceeding and agency and their share of dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of time from assignment to decision (time-to-decision buckets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables V and VI report time from assignment to examiner to issuance of examiner's decision, in buckets: 'One month or less', '1 month but not more than 3 months', '3 months but not more than 6 months', '6 months but not more than 12 months', 'More than 12 months'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-to-decision is reported separately for cases decided by shortened procedure versus those decided after evidentiary hearings, allowing direct comparison of processing speed by disposition method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of shortened-procedure vs evidentiary-hearing cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-tabulated counts comparing number and age/time-to-decision distributions for 'Shortened Proc.' cases (decided on written submissions only) and 'Evidentiary Hrg.' cases (decided on the merits after hearings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables evaluation of the efficiency impact of shortened procedures; Tables V and related text present these comparisons (e.g., counts per time bucket for each method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate totals and agency-level totals (Grand totals / 21 agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grand totals aggregating counts across the 21 reporting agencies (e.g., 'GRAND TOTALS - 21 AGENCIES' for pending, new, disposed, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an overall picture of examiner workload and dispositions across the federal government; individual agency totals appear in rows and subtotals appear per agency section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes, special-case annotations, and data caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory footnotes and annotations (examples: 'In 1 case the hearing was recessed pending further order of the Commission.'; 'Includes 76 cases "disposed of" by consolidation.'; 'Examiner decision waived under Rule III(e).'; 'Data available do not indicate how many of these cases were assigned to examiners prior to July 1, 1956.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notes indicate exceptions, counting rules, waivers, default cases, consolidations, differences in agency counting practices, and other caveats critical to correct interpretation of the tabular metrics.
